messages.author: 863a0481c01d0ecd
messages.subject: Infinite values when summary.fitted.values
parts:
Hello,

I have a problem when I run the model below that includes spatial and temporal terms, The summary looks normal but I obtain infinite and very large numbers (e.g. 5346661268800091458370000512782999075422208) when retrieving mod$summary.fitted.values$mean. This does not happen when I use a cheap model with no spatial and temporal components as I also show below. Would anyone help me figuring out why this is happening? I attach here the data and the graph file.

Any help would be much appreciated.

Thanks,

Victor.

Problematic model with Infinite and very large numbers in mod$summary.fittted.values$mean:
formula  = y~ x + xsq + w + x:w +  f(INLA_ID, model="bym", graph=inla.read.graph("zones.graph"), adjust.for.con.comp = FALSE) +  f(year.struct, model= "ar1") + f(year, model= "iid")
mod = inla(formula, data=load("data.RData"), family="poisson", verbose=TRUE, control.fixed=list(prec.intercept=0.1), control.predictor = list(compute=TRUE), control.compute=list(dic=TRUE, cpo=TRUE), E=(weight)) 

Non problematic model:
formula = y~ x + xsq + w + x:w
cheap.mod = inla(formula, data=data, family="poisson", verbose=TRUE, control.fixed=list(prec.intercept=0.1, expand.factor.strategy='inla'), control.inla=list(strategy="gaussian", int.strategy="eb"), control.predictor = list(compute=TRUE), control.compute=list(dic=TRUE, cpo=TRUE), E=(weight))

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Infinite values when summary.fitted.values
parts:
On Thu, 2016-04-07 at 13:59 -0700, Víctor Hugo Gutiérrez Vélez wrote:
> Thank you Havard. I had posted them in my original message but here
> are them again :)
>

Hi,

as you see from the plot, the issue seems to be related to that so many
nodes in the graph for the bym model does not have any neigbours or
only 1, and the confounding eith f(year.struct,...) which you do not
need really (its a constant)

Precision for year.struct                 1.100e-03 



when the marginal stdev are so high, there is usually some
counfounding, in the sense that you could have 

intercept + one

and you can add/subtract a constant to any one of these. 

H

******************


load("data.RData")
formula  = y~ x + xsq + w + x:w +  f(INLA_ID, model="bym",
graph="zones.graph", adjust.for.con.comp = FALSE) +
f(year.struct, model= "ar1") + f(year, model= "iid")

r = inla(formula, data=data, family="poisson",
    verbose=TRUE, 
    control.fixed=list(prec.intercept=0.1),
    control.inla = list(strategy = "gaussian",  h=0.001), 
    control.predictor = list(compute=TRUE),
    ##control.compute=list(dic=TRUE, cpo=TRUE),
    E=weight)

g = inla.read.graph("zones.graph")
plot(r$summary.linear.predictor$sd, g$nnbs[data$INLA_ID])

plot(r$summary.random$INLA_ID$sd[1:g$n], g$nnbs)
--
Håvard Rue
he...@r-inla.org

messages.subject: Re: Infinite values when summary.fitted.values
parts:
Thank you Havard. Yes, there are some nodes that are more connected than others. That is the nature of the data. 

I re-ran the model without year.struct and it still has the same issue. Given this situation, I have two questions: 1) can I rely on the parameter estimates from this model even with this situation?  2) is there any way to obtain reliable estimates of summary.fitted.values for disconnected or poorly connected nodes? An easy but non rigorous way I could think of is to run a model without spatial and temporal terms and obtain the estimates for disconnected nodes from there and then use the spatial and temporal model to get the estimates for the rest. Could you think on a more elegant option?

Thank you.

Victor.
